info.title: Klavi Experts API
info.description:
The HTTP API of a Klavi Experts installation.

## Authentication

Send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer sk-...`. `X-API-Key: sk-...` is
also accepted, but send exactly ONE of them — the gateway checks
`Authorization` first and that check is terminal, so a stale bearer token
decides the request even when a valid key is present in the other header.

A key is a full user identity on the install. It belongs on a server. For
anything browser-facing, mint a session token with
`POST /api/v1/public/sessions`.

## Streaming

`POST /api/v1/conversations/chat` returns `application/x-ndjson` over plain
HTTP — one JSON object per line, terminated by one carrying `done: true`. No
WebSocket is required.

Two things about it surprise people:

* **Sending a message is three calls.** `/chat` never CREATES message rows; it
  updates one you make first. Create the user's turn and an assistant
  placeholder with `POST /api/v1/responses/`, then pass the placeholder's uid
  as `response`. Omit it and the model still answers, but nothing persists.
* **HTTP 200 is not proof of an answer.** Generation reports its own failures
  in the terminal event's `error` field, not in the status code.

Durations in the terminal event are NANOSECONDS.

## Errors

`403` with `{"error": "license_expired"}` is an installation-level failure,
not a permission problem: nothing about the request is wrong, and only the
install's administrator can resolve it.

BearerKey.description: Your `sk-` API key, or a browser session token.

ApiKey.name: X-API-Key
ApiKey.description: Legacy header. Never send it alongside Authorization — the bearer check wins.

AdoptContextRequest.title: AdoptContextRequest
AdoptContextRequest.description:
Request to link already-embedded documents into a conversation's hidden
upload collection, matched by content hash.

Fields:
- `conversation_uid`: The conversation whose upload collection should
receive the documents (created on first adoption).
- `keys`: Context keys — SHA-256 content hashes for file attachments.
Non-document keys (e.g. web-page URLs) are skipped, not errors.

queues a webhook reponse as a callback once the process has completed.

Fields:
- `status`: int, HTTP status code for the request
- `message`: str, status response message

Inherited:
- `timestamp`: int, the current UTC datetime in Epoch millis

ContextEmbedding.title: ContextEmbedding
ContextEmbedding.description:
Conversation-context embedding row for the unified `context_embedding`
table (migration 026). `vector` holds the raw model-native embedding —
that is what serializes into ConversationTextEmbeddingResponse, keeping
the response identical to the pre-matryoshka API. The stored row differs:
storeContextEmbedding writes the padded/truncated normalised 2048-dim
form plus the 256-dim mrl vector, tagged with `embedding_model_id` so
searches only compare distances within one model's vector space.

#### Fields:
- `group_key`: str, the grouping key for this conversation max 200 chars.
- `ctx_action`: ContextDispatchAction, docs, web, video, image etc
- `split_text`: str, single chunk of split text
- `token_length`: int, token count from the embedding model's tokenizer

#### Inherited:
- `uid`: UUID4,
- `created_at`: int, epoch unix millis utc
- `updated_at`: int, epoch unix millis utc
- `embedding_model_id`: int FK public.embedding_model(id),
- `vector`: list[float], raw model-native embedding (any supported dim)
- `mrl_vector`: list[float] | None, normalised 'short' vector representation
- `mrl_dims`: int = 256, dimensionality of normalised vector representation

ConversationForkRequest.title: ConversationForkRequest
ConversationForkRequest.description:
Fork (branch) a conversation into a new one.

title        — name for the fork; empty → server generates a fresh
               summary of the transcript (fallback "<title> V2").
response_uid — branch point: copy messages up to and including this
               response. None copies the whole conversation.
target_user  — fork into another user's account (the source stays with
               the caller). None/self keeps the fork in the caller's.

ConversationTextEmbeddingRequest.title: ConversationTextEmbeddingRequest
ConversationTextEmbeddingRequest.description:
Similar to a `TextEmbeddingRequest` but adds contextual data fields for
storage in the context dispatch embeddings [cache] table.

Fields:
- All inherited from baseclasses and mixins

Inherited:
- `group_key`: str, a unique key for a conversation's embeddings
- `ctx_action`: ContextDispatchAction, one of the context types
- `append_to_existing`: bool, flag to indicate if we append the request to
the context at `group_key` or delete it first.
- `run_in_background`: bool, if specified and True, runs the request in a
background task, otherwise runs inline and returns a result.

- `texts`: A list of texts to return embeddings for
- `split_strategy_id`: An optional split strategy id. If supplied, each item
in the `texts` array will be split before being embedded. If a split strategy
id is supplied but doesn't exist in the database, the default will used.

- `user_uid`: The logged in user id, if running in a permissioned system
- `ml_model_name`: The identifier of the ML model to process the request
- `webhook`: optional webhook specifier, reserved for future use

ConversationTextEmbeddingResponse.title: ConversationTextEmbeddingResponse

Fields:
- `data`: A list of `ContextEmbedding` objects

DocumentEmbeddingRequest.title: DocumentEmbeddingRequest
DocumentEmbeddingRequest.description:
The Document Embedding Post Request model contains a list of files and
folders to be embedded. An optional Collection Name may be provided and
if so, the files and folders referenced, should also be linked to the
collection, which should be created if needed.

Fields:
- `collection`: The name or UUID of a collection to add this req into or None
if the (entire) upload shouldn't be added to a collection. The parameter will
be tested for a valid UUID, if this fails, it will be treated as a name.
Also supply `auto_create_collection=true` if you supply a name and want
to create a new Collection with this name if one doesn't already exist (for
the logged in user). The request will fail if `collection` is supplied, is
a name, `auto_create_collection` is not supplied or False and an
associated collection could not be found.
- `auto_create_collection`: Bool (default=False). If a collection name
is supplied and auto_create... is false, raises an error if the named collection
wasn't found in the database (for the current user).
- `min_role_id`: int (default=None) The permission level for the uploaded
document. If unspecified the user's role should be applied as default.

Inherited:
- `split_strategy_id`: One of the pre-saved text split strategies to apply
a text split size & overlap to the embedding. Optional, defaults to 1, the
strategy included in the application setup.
- `files_and_folders`: List of absolute paths containing either a reference
to a single file or to a folder. Folders will be expanded internally to
create file paths for allowed file extensions.
- `upload_flavor`: One of the `DocUploadFlavorId` enum values. E.g.
`conversation` or `collection` etc. Default is `collection`. This creates
a filter on document-collection-link(s) so that document groupings can be
used in different contexts.

- `user_uid`: The logged in user id, if running in a permissioned system
- `ml_model_name`: The name of the embedding model to process the request
- `job_queue_run_id`: Allows the user to add a subsequent request to a prior
one. If not suppplied a new `runId` will be created so that files in a given
request can be batched together (for progress reporting and containment).
- `webhook`: optional webhook specifier, reserved for future use

DocumentSearchDiagnostics.title: DocumentSearchDiagnostics
DocumentSearchDiagnostics.description:
What the fused search actually did, for the info popover on the results.

A fused ranking is opaque by construction — the user sees an order and has
no way to tell whether a result is there because it was named that, said
that, or meant that, nor whether the vector channel ran at all. This is the
answer to "why am I seeing this?", and to "why am I NOT seeing this?" —
which is the harder question and the reason the dropped-stopword list and
the relevance floor are both in here.

DocumentSearchItem.title: DocumentSearchItem
DocumentSearchItem.description:
A SourceDocument as returned by the fused document search.

Distinct from `SemanticSearchDocumentItem` because the relevance fields are
OPTIONAL here. The fused search has a lexical channel that can match a
document on its file name alone, and a file name is never embedded — such a
row has no split, no cosine distance and therefore no honest score. Forcing
a number onto it would put a percentage in the UI that means nothing.

LibraryBrowseResponse.title: LibraryBrowseResponse
LibraryBrowseResponse.description:
One level of a Library's folder tree.

`is_library` is false for a plain collection, which has no watched root and
therefore no tree — the caller should fall back to the flat document list

LibraryFile.title: LibraryFile
LibraryFile.description:
A file sitting directly in the folder being browsed.

`relative_path` is its place in the library; `source_path` is the absolute
disk path (filesystem libraries) or the opaque provider URI (cloud), kept
for a reveal-on-disk affordance and for support diagnosing a bad sync.

LibraryFolder.title: LibraryFolder
LibraryFolder.description:
A child folder inside a Library, with a RECURSIVE file count — a folder
reports everything beneath it, not just its immediate children, because a
count that stopped at one level would read as 0 for the deep project trees
these libraries are made of.

LibrarySearchHit.title: LibrarySearchHit
LibrarySearchHit.description:
One file row from a merged library search.

`match_reasons` is why this row is here — 'path' (its name or folder
matched), 'lexical' (its text contains the terms), 'vector' (it means the
same thing). Surfaced because the three answer genuinely different
questions and a user scanning results deserves to know which one fired.

LibrarySearchResponse.title: LibrarySearchResponse
LibrarySearchResponse.description: Merged (name/path + lexical + vector) search across one library.

SimilaritySearchCTXRequest.title: SimilaritySearchCTXRequest

Similarity search request for context dispatch embeddings. Searches text
splits with the specified `group_keys` returning results conforming to the
`top_k` & `temperature` parameters.

Fields:
- `group_keys`: list[str], the grouping keys in the context dispatch embedding table

Inherited (BasePostRequest):
- `user_uid`: The logged in user id, if running in a permissioned system
- `ml_model_name`: The identifier of the ML model to process the request
- `webhook`: optional webhook specifier, reserved for future use

Inherited (SimilaritySearchBaseRequest):
- `split_strategy_id`: The split strategy (text size/overlap) to use
- `prompt`: The source text to use for the search
- `top_k`: Number of document chunks to return
- `temperature`: How similar the search results need to be
- `context_size`: Maximum context size of the LLM, will restrict the number
of items returned to fit into the context, if specified. Reserved for
future use.

TODO:

post.description:
Speaks the OpenAI chat-completions protocol, so a stock `openai` client works unmodified with `baseURL` pointed here and `model` set to an expert's uid.

Retrieval still happens: source documents and retrieval metrics come back under a `klavi` key on the final chunk.

Differences from OpenAI: `n > 1`, `response_format` and caller-supplied `tools` are refused rather than ignored, because silently returning one choice or prose-instead-of-JSON is a wrong answer the caller cannot see. A conversation also carries memory of the API key's owner, so this is not stateless in the way OpenAI is.

model.description: An expert uid, `expert:<uid>`, `raw:<uid>` for the bare model, or a unique expert name.

klavi.description: Extensions: `conversation` to continue one, `include_thinking` to receive reasoning.

200.description: A completion, or an SSE stream
The experts this key may use

get.description:
Return a list of the current collections to the caller.
Pass ?exclude_smart=true to hide collections linked to smart collections.
Pass ?exclude_conversation=false to include conversation collections.
System-managed collections (per-project resource collections) are
hidden by default; pass ?include_system_managed=true to include them.

post.description:
Add a new collection using the data in the specified partial. Returns the
newly created Collection if successful, raises 422 otherwise

Stop a detached generation. Client disconnects no longer cancel the
model (generation is deliberately connection-independent), so the Stop
button calls this to actually halt it. The cancelled task persists its
partial text and publishes a done event on the conversation stream.

Fork (branch) a conversation into a new one.

Copies messages up to and including body.response_uid (or all of them),
optionally into another user's account (fork-to-teammate — the source
conversation stays with the caller, and the fork carries forked_by
lineage so the recipient's UI can say who sent it).
Suggested name for a fork of this conversation.

get.description: Token usage summary for a conversation, scoped to the calling user.

Return a list of documents that the user has permission to view. These will
be either owned by or at the same or lower role as, the logged in user.
To retrive documents from a collection, specify a `collection` param as a UUID.
To further filter [search] by keyword(s) in the document name, title or summary
add a `searchTerm` param containing the keyword(s) to filter by. If limit
and/or skip are specified they are always applied as filters as the last
operations on the query to allow for paging.

Returns
A data object containing a list of matching documents.

List the model profiles this user may see.

Visibility is `_visible_to` — see it for the rule. In short: a user sees
shared experts at or below their role, plus everything they own; admins
see the whole shared surface; nobody but the owner sees an owner-only
("Only me") expert. The chat expert-picker reads the same list, so this
is also what scopes which experts a user can chat with — if none are
visible the client falls back to the site default model.

post.description:
Exchange a server-held API key for a short-lived credential safe to hand to one browser. The token is bound to one expert, one conversation and one origin, carries the guest role, and expires within 15 minutes.

The expert must be guest-visible (`min_role_id <= 1`, not private). One that is not is refused here rather than silently answering on the site default model with no persona and no knowledge.

The origin must already be registered against the API key.

400.description: Unregistered origin, or an expert a guest cannot use

503.description: This install has no Redis, so cannot issue sessions

404.description: No such session for this key

post.description: Submit structured feedback on a response. Stores as a PREFERENCE memory.
